clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old female presented with a 1-month history of moderate continuous low-back pain and a long-standing right lower cervical lymph node (2×2.5 cm, mobile, non-tender, firm) present for over 20 years, reportedly stable. She had prior right-sided upper neck surgery 35 years ago. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) with cell-block of the cervical lymph node was performed. Cytomorphological examination revealed cellular smears with tumor cells dispersed singly and in loose clusters within a chondromyxoid stroma. The tumor cells were round to polygonal with mild pleomorphism, eccentrically placed nuclei, coarse chromatin, occasional prominent nucleoli, and moderate cytoplasm with some cytoplasmic vacuolations. Occasional loose clusters of smaller cells with scant cytoplasm were also noted. Immunohistochemistry on the cell-block demonstrated strong diffuse membranous positivity for CK7 in luminal cells (epithelial marker) and strong nuclear positivity for p63 in abluminal cells (myoepithelial marker), with less than 10% of tumor cells showing nuclear positivity for GATA3. Based on the cytomorphological features and immunohistochemical findings, a final diagnosis of metastatic epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma was established.
